text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in the Swedish papers on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Prices of houses in Stockholm have fallen 20 percent since the start of the 1980s and are now at a record low.
- Swedish nurses were lining up at unemployment agencies to register for nursing jobs in Norway.
- Volvo managing director Soren Gyll denies there is any power struggle between him and Volvo board head Bert-Olof Svanholm.
- A merger by Handelsbanken and S-E-Banken would have to be approved by the European Union's competition authority.
- State venture capital provider Nutek says wind power will be a viable energy source in the future.

- Shares in S-E-Banken and Handelsbanken rose on Monday on an otherwise weaker Swedish sharemarket on a report that the two banks were in talks about a possible merger. S-E-Banken has the most to win through a merger.
- A majority of local politicians including Stockholm city mayor Mats Hulth are in favour of closing Stockholm's city airport, Bromma. A decision will be made soon.
- U.S. investment fund Fidelity Investments raised its stake in Swedish vehicle maker Volvo with a purchase of 3.5 million shares to total 28.3 million in the first half of the year.

- Swedish construction and real estate company Skanska has rented all of its 45,000-square-metre Thomas More Square office complex, with Reuters taking the last 10,000 square metres. Skanska is considering selling the building.
